```sh
  --title "U.S. economic briefing" \
  --selection "$FRED_ROOT/examples/macro-selection.json"

starforge fred import --project "$FRED_PROJECT" \
  --id macro-original --expected-revision 1 \
  --source "$FRED_ROOT/examples/briefing-20261012/macro-source.capture.json"

starforge fred briefing-preview --project "$FRED_PROJECT" \
  --capture 4c7fc88552da69b9448054334bad10b72afee056ed93bcd2fb741d698dde042c \
  --briefing-file "$FRED_ROOT/examples/macro-briefing.json"

starforge fred review --project "$FRED_PROJECT" \
  --id macro-briefing-review --expected-revision 2 \
  --capture 4c7fc88552da69b9448054334bad10b72afee056ed93bcd2fb741d698dde042c \
  --note "$FRED_ROOT/examples/briefing-20261012/review-note.txt" \
  --briefing-file "$FRED_ROOT/examples/macro-briefing.json"

starforge fred briefing --project "$FRED_PROJECT" \
  --review af00af636c9397ac146966fed06588ef531594c65bc1ec289eada76b4af97802

starforge fred briefing-file --project "$FRED_PROJECT" \
  --review af00af636c9397ac146966fed06588ef531594c65bc1ec289eada76b4af97802 \
```

The capture ID is `4c7fc88552da69b9448054334bad10b72afee056ed93bcd2fb741d698dde042c`; the unchanged note and selection produce review `af00af636c9397ac146966fed06588ef531594c65bc1ec289eada76b4af97802`. The original native importer verifies the captured source. The report command reads the saved review, and the file command writes its full original HTML.

To continue an existing project, reopen it and read its current revision and retained operation IDs. Do not apply these fresh-project revisions to another project's current state. After an interrupted mutation, inspect/reconcile the same original operation before choosing another ID.


## Publish and deliver to a customer

Use **Merchant** in that original project to select the saved review, your existing merchant HTTPS origin and approved native payment profile. Publication advertises the original dataset and complete HTML/CSV/JSON/manifest assets. # Economic workspace clients and agents

Operate a retained FRED economic product from the installed command, a typed JavaScript client, or the existing authenticated merchant MCP host. All three paths attach to the original economic workspace: the same project, source captures, reviews, publication, merchant listener, configured SF88 buyer and saved customer intents.

The client covers official source intake, complete public-table imports, combined macro editions, observations and revision comparisons, projection review, publication, merchant control, customer preparation/execution/recovery, complete downloads and project receiving. The MCP family contains 30 tools and loads its runtime only when that configured family is used.

## Start or reconnect the original workspace

Use Node 24 and the existing economic application installation. The original workspace owner starts its same project with the configured buyer and facilitator:

~~~sh
starforge fred serve \
  --project /PRIVATE/ORIGINAL_FRED_PROJECT \
  --buyer-config /PRIVATE/ORIGINAL_BUYER.json \
  --facilitator https://ORIGINAL-FACILITATOR \
  --merchant-port ORIGINAL_MERCHANT_PORT \
  --connection-file /PRIVATE/fred-console.json
~~~

The capitalized paths, origin and port select the operator's existing resources. The optional connection-file flag writes the actual startup record with owner-only permissions. It includes the native project ID, complete launch binding and private session URL. On a later start of the same project, the record is replaced atomically; an existing record belonging to another project is rejected. The original managed Application may also supply its retained complete startup record directly.

The workspace binding covers its canonical project directory and creation identity, selected buyer configuration hash/path, facilitator, local-facilitator setting and merchant port. The client reads the native launch endpoint and compares the exact binding before it dispatches a workspace operation. A declared expected binding adds a fixed operator selection. A connection-record rotation reconnects the client to the same project using its current session.

Create the installed client connection using the existing original public payment file:

~~~sh
starforge fred-workspace connection-init \
  --out /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --console-url-file /PRIVATE/fred-console.json \
  --workspace macro \
  --inputs-file stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/examples/fred-workspace-inputs.json \
  --payment-file /PRIVATE/ORIGINAL_PUBLIC_PAYMENT.json \
  --merchant-origin https://ORIGINAL-MERCHANT-HOST \
  --profile native
starforge fred-workspace status --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json
~~~

The connection initializer authenticates an actual launch read before publishing its private connection file. Its returned projectId, bindingSha256 and instanceId identify that original server. Use an existing profiles JSON file with --profiles-file when there are several merchant configurations.

For a complete source checkout the supplied input-alias example resolves directly to the retained UNRATE, CPIAUCSL and GDP source files. Within an installed distribution these same files sit under its source directory. Input aliases are resolved from the input-alias file's directory. Client configuration paths are resolved from the connection file's directory.

The connection schema is stellar-forge.fred-workspace-connection.v1. Each workspace has one consoleUrlFile or consoleUrlEnv reference, optional projectId and expectedBindingSha256, request capacity/time settings, inputs, and merchantProfiles. The file or environment variable retains the original startup JSON or unchanged private URL. A bare URL requires the explicit original projectId. Credential values stay in the original private workspace and buyer configuration.

## Build and review a real macro edition

Read status and inputs first. input-inspect reads the complete selected source file, returning its file SHA256, original publisher-table URL, retrieval time, series ID and original table byte/hash metadata. The configured input digest, when present, is checked again during import.

~~~sh
starforge fred-workspace inputs --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json
starforge fred-workspace input-inspect --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json --input unrate
starforge fred-workspace import --connection /PRIVATE/fred-client.json \
  --input unrate --id ORIGINAL_IMPORT_ID --revision CURRENT_REVISION --sha256 ORIGINAL_FILE_SHA256
~~~

Continue with the revision and captureId returned by each original operation. Import the declared CPI and GDP files in the same way, then combine their retained capture IDs:

~~~js
import {
  FredWorkspaceClient, readFredWorkspaceConfiguration, saveFredFile
} from './stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/fred-workspace-client.mjs';

const configured = await readFredWorkspaceConfiguration('/PRIVATE/fred-client.json');
const client = new FredWorkspaceClient(configured.workspaces.macro);
try {
  const state = await client.state();
  const captureId = state.project.selectedCapture;
  let offset = 0;
  do {
    const page = await client.observations({ captureId, series: 'UNRATE', offset });
    // Consume page.rows with their original date, value, missing flag and units.

  const retained = await saveFredFile(client, { kind: 'project' }, '/PRIVATE/project-copy.json');
  console.log({ projectId: retained.projectId, bytes: retained.bytes, sha256: retained.sha256 });
} finally {
  client.close();
}
~~~

## Source and calculation contract

The calculation uses the original source level values. It keeps every observation's series, date, literal value, missing marker, frequency, units, seasonal adjustment, information date and time basis. It does not resample observations or substitute a missing value.

| Selection | Exact baseline |
| --- | --- |
| Previous period: monthly | Same calendar day, one month earlier |
| Previous period: quarterly | Same calendar day, three months earlier |
| Previous period: semiannual / annual | Same calendar day, six / twelve months earlier |
| Previous period: daily / weekly / biweekly | One / seven / fourteen calendar days earlier |
| Year earlier | Same calendar day twelve months earlier; monthly, quarterly, semiannual or annual series |
| Previous observation | Immediately preceding original observation row, including a missing marker |

Baselines come from the same retained capture and may precede the displayed interval. A missing exact calendar date remains absent; a prior missing observation remains missing. Daily or irregular series can use **previous observation** to request that explicitly. Previous-period calendar comparisons retain holidays and other absent dates as absent baselines.

Absolute change is exact decimal subtraction. For a series whose original unit is **Percent**, this difference is labeled **Percentage points**. Other differences retain the original unit.

Relative percent change is separately selected and uses `100 × (current − baseline) / baseline`. The calculation uses integer decimal arithmetic, then rounds to the selected 0–12 decimal places using half-even rounding. The output retains whether rounding occurred. A zero denominator produces `ZERO_BASE` with no numeric relative result.

The [BLS percent-change guide](https://www.bls.gov/cpi/factsheets/calculating-percent-changes.htm) explains the same two-observation formula, matching months for twelve-month changes, and consistent index bases. The original [FRED observations API](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/series_observations.html) provides the source values and real-time fields used by API captures. Public table imports retain their actual table retrieval dates.

CPIAUCSL is an index series. Its absolute difference is in its original index units; its relative change is a percentage. GDP in the starter is nominal quarterly GDP in billions of dollars at a seasonally adjusted annual rate. The report keeps those original units; a quarter-to-quarter relative comparison is the direct ratio of those two published values. It does not annualize that growth rate or convert nominal values to real values.

| Measure state | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `READY` | Both original observations have supported numeric values |
| `SOURCE_MISSING` | The selected current observation has its original missing marker |
| `BASE_ABSENT` | The selected baseline row is outside or absent from the retained source |
| `BASE_MISSING` | The exact baseline has its original missing marker |
| `CALENDAR_DATE_ABSENT` | The selected earlier calendar date does not exist |
| `NUMERIC_LITERAL_UNSUPPORTED` | The original value cannot be interpreted by the supported decimal grammar |

Relative results additionally report `NOT_SELECTED`, `ZERO_BASE` or `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`. The complete CSV includes both the absolute and relative states.

A briefing selects 1–50 original series and 1–10,000 original observations. The complete source capture remains retained even when the reporting window selects fewer rows. A single native asset is limited to 16 MiB and the publication's combined asset budget is 64 MiB. All four briefing files must fit; the application gives a capacity error before advertising an incomplete report.

## Import the three series into one project

Run these commands from the installed source directory `stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/fred`. Keep the private project outside the installed package. A new project finishes these imports at revision 4 with three retained capture IDs. Each import reports its original capture ID and current revision. When using an existing project, read its current revision with `node cli.mjs show --project /absolute/private/macro-project` and use the actual revision for the next operation.

Open **Editions & review → Combine retained public tables**. Select the CPIAUCSL, GDP and UNRATE captures and choose **Create combined edition**. The resulting capture contains all 2,219 original observations under one retained source identity. Inspect it and save its review.

The same operation is available through the CLI. Use the three capture IDs returned by the original imports:

```sh
node cli.mjs combine --project /absolute/private/macro-project \
  --id macro-combined-20261012 --expected-revision 4 \
  --captures CPI_CAPTURE_SHA,GDP_CAPTURE_SHA,UNRATE_CAPTURE_SHA
```

The command returns the combined capture ID and revision 5. Subsequent reviews and publications use that current revision. When continuing an existing project, use its actual revision and saved operation IDs. You can also review and publish any of the original single-series captures independently. **Merchant** publishes a reviewed edition with the host's existing payment terms and facilitator. **Customer** prepares the exact published request and receives the original paid response. The [application guide](../README.md#publish-and-operate-the-merchant) covers merchant lifetime, native purchase, recovery, pagination and complete project receiving.

Public-table editions retain the UTC retrieval date in `as_of` and `PUBLIC_TABLE_RETRIEVAL_DATE` in `time_basis`. FRED API captures use the selected real-time period and `FRED_REALTIME_DATE`. Both modes preserve their own source metadata in the retained capture and published manifest.

## Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs builds open-source, self-hostable software for a merchant to sell a useful API, dataset or agent operation on Stellar and for its buyer to receive the complete result in an existing application. It connects the exact approved request, native transfer, usable output and merchant fulfillment. That connection survives interrupted delivery, source changes and handover to another maintainer.

We request **$38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance**. The funded outcome is **two independently operated merchant services and two independent buyer operators**: installed services by day 30, recurring testnet use by day 90, and both merchants operating maintainable mainnet services by day 150. T2 runs the same useful service through two independently operated testnet facilitators.

The working product supplies the completed foundation. Funding pays for the remaining source and receiving adaptations, Stellar deployment, monitoring and recovery improvements required by the two selected services. Reusable improvements return to the public product.

## Customer problem, need and adoption

Our first customer is a recurring API or data-service operator, or an agency implementing that service in a customer's application. The commissioning payer buys installation and handover; an independent buyer pays for the useful resource. These roles may belong to different organizations.

A paid response alone may leave an analyst without the full population, original units, observation period or usable report. A multi-step agent task can exceed its budget even when each payment is valid. The merchant must connect accepted customer output to its offer, fulfillment and accounting. Our product carries the source, aggregate approval, all agreed output and operating state through that whole task.

Two installation patterns define the funded work:

- **Recurring report:** a merchant publishes a reviewed economic or operational report. The buyer acquires a new period or source edition, compares it with the prior result, and opens the report and selected data in its application.
- **Typed dataset or saved query:** the buyer approves a distinct query or refreshed population and receives every agreed paid page and file, with the original request, source selection, aggregate cost and merchant records.

The two funded installations and agreements remain to be selected. Existing conversations clarify the commercial route: Veridex invited the buyer CLI into its testnet cohort and reported no third-party testing budget; CoCart's founder asked who introduces, pays and contracts for customer work; Blockscout expressed interest and reported no integration budget; Nansen declined. Completed source and receiving implementations demonstrate delivery capability; independent customer adoption is a funded outcome.

Each selected workorder fixes the payer, merchant, buyer, receiving engineer, authorized source, geography or population, period, query, complete output, priced unit, spending limit, host and acceptance owner. The first installed execution establishes the operating baseline. A later source period, edition or distinct useful query supplies recurring work. The receiving engineer performs an actual change or recovery before handover.

The purchase target follows selected buyer demand. Two buyers purchasing once each ordinary weekday generate twenty purchases in fourteen days. Their T3 workorders must establish useful demand for at least thirty distinct paid requests across both buyers and merchants during that window. Additional purchases must correspond to useful source periods, queries or the complete advertised pages and files needed by those tasks. A retry, saved-result reopen or cached use remains part of its original purchase.

TokenJunkieLabs earns implementation fees and separately scoped care; merchants retain resource receipts and implementation partners retain customer relationships. Customer-specific adaptations share one capacity and cost allocation with grant work. Existing proposed commercial workshares become cash resources only when their actual payment terms and collections support that treatment.

## Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar supplies native authorization and settlement for a reviewed purchase. In the x402 Exact flow, the buyer signs a Soroban token-transfer authorization binding payer, recipient, atomic amount and expiration. A facilitator submits it on the selected network; an explicit sponsorship policy can cover transaction fees. We use existing Stellar SDKs and token contracts.

The application retains the exact HTTP endpoint and method or MCP tool and arguments, source selection, payment alternative, complete output and fulfillment history. It checks the approved operation before dispatch and joins these records to the native transaction. Wallet authority and aggregate spending remain with the buyer; source, pricing and fulfillment authority remain with the merchant.

Existing foundations already provide substantial capabilities. Stellar's x402 client libraries handle payment challenges, Soroban authorization and signed retries; the Stellar CLI supplies the signing identity. Facilitators verify and settle, and Bazaar publishes resource schemas. ApiCharge's published proxy/access-grant approach provides typed paid access and retained purchased service levels. MPP Router provides paid proxy access, request-ID response caching and signed job polling.

Our proposed **Open Track** contribution is the reusable merchant-to-customer workflow around those foundations: complete acquired data and reports in the customer's editable application, exact source/query and aggregate task approval, all agreed pages and files, original-payment recovery, merchant accounting and another engineer's maintainable installation. The six funded packages implement that workflow in two independent services and publish the resulting improvements. The original relationship among source, approval, distinct native transfers, output and accounting survives changes of provider, source edition or receiving operator. Open Track fit rests on this contribution and its measured usefulness; track selection remains subject to the issuer's invitation and review. Native payments, returning independent buyers and complete customer tasks measure the ecosystem value. The retained Vellar/Periplo comparison found no shared seller/route identity; registration and compatibility for the same selected service remain part of the funded work.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

Six connected components carry the customer task:

1. **Merchant workspace:** a private operator selects an authorized source edition or named query, schema, output and limits. Source or terms changes become separately reviewed states.
2. **HTTP or MCP resource:** adapters preserve types, nulls, keys, pagination, units, time basis and snapshot or live behavior. Customer-controlled credential references govern source access.
3. **Buyer approval and budget:** the buyer approves the exact method or tool, arguments, source scope and payment choice. The original challenge and remote schema must match before signing; per-payment limits and existing reservations govern aggregate spending.
4. **Stellar settlement:** the native signer and facilitator use the reviewed network, asset, recipient, amount, expiry and fee policy. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transfer. The existing MPP Charge integration retains its own challenge and recovery lifecycle.
5. **Complete delivery and accounting:** all agreed pages and files, original attempts, accepted output, merchant notification and acknowledgment remain connected. A saved prepaid call retains its selected pass and consumed allowance when defaults change.
6. **Recovery and receiving:** confirmation, transfer, output and fulfillment retain separate states. An uncertain response is reconciled against its original dispatch. Another engineer restores configuration, history and customer files, supplies authorized secret references and continues the original work.

The implemented buyer workflow searches declared catalog inputs, follows complete page continuation and keeps the original provider page, row and payment selection. The buyer enters explicit HTTP path/query values or MCP arguments. A configured native workspace binds the concrete request, body and spending cap to one durable intent, then supports execution, recovery, scoped history and complete saved-response download.

The [complete financial walkthrough](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/2d1854f4b148b41d8c96bc0f8de2924faa2a8f84/stellar-forge/developer-site/dist/grant-data/financial-walkthrough.md) carries the same customer from the paid result through quote/invoice review, actual Stellar or bank receiving, dated allocations, refunds, reconciliation and customer close. Purchase principal, fees, commercial valuation, issued obligations and later service activity retain their own records.

Node.js supplies browser, CLI, typed-client and MCP interfaces; source and receiving applications also use Python/SQLite and PHP/WordPress/WooCommerce. T2 configures the same service for two compatible testnet facilitators. T3 deploys each merchant's reviewed mainnet configuration. The selected service workorders determine the actual remaining source and receiving adaptations. The x402 Exact integration uses existing Stellar token contracts. ## Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar supplies authorization and settlement for the selected purchase. In the existing x402 Exact flow, the buyer signs token-transfer authorization binding payer, recipient, atomic amount and expiration. A facilitator submits it on the selected network; fee sponsorship can cover the transaction fee. We use existing Stellar SDKs and token contracts.

Our application binds that transfer to the exact HTTP request or MCP tool/arguments, selected source, payment option, complete customer output and fulfillment history. The buyer controls wallet authority and total spend; the merchant controls source access, pricing and fulfillment.

The ecosystem already supplies substantial infrastructure. Stellar's x402 client libraries handle payment challenges, Soroban authorization and signed retries; the Stellar CLI supplies the signing identity. Facilitators verify and settle, and Bazaar describes discoverable resources. ApiCharge's published proxy/access-grant approach provides typed paid access and retained purchased service levels. MPP Router provides paid proxy access, request-ID response caching and signed job polling. Our proposed Open Track contribution is a reusable way to keep an entire paid customer task coherent across those components: the reviewed source and query, aggregate approval, distinct native transfers, every agreed page/file, editable output, interrupted-delivery recovery, accounting and independent maintenance. The application retains the original relationship among those records when a provider, source edition or receiving operator changes. The two customer installations develop the remaining source/consumer and deployment joins and return reusable improvements to that public workflow. Open Track fit rests on this technical and customer-operation contribution and its measured usefulness; the selected track remains subject to the issuer’s invitation and review.

The programme makes that contribution measurable. It installs two independent services and buyers, operates the same useful service through two testnet facilitators, and carries both merchants into recurring mainnet use. The two-provider comparison holds the service, schema, source population and useful output constant. Existing catalogs do not by themselves establish this compatibility: the retained Vellar/Periplo comparison found no shared seller/route identity, so explicit registration and integration of the same service is part of the funded work.

Each installation records its source edition, authority, network/facilitator, protected records, observable signals, thresholds, notification destinations and primary/backup responders. The assessment covers altered offers or approvals, wrong payment/output attribution, unauthorized access, interrupted fulfillment, missing observations and restoration of the wrong generation. Application-level observation covers source and delivery failures.

The two operated response cases retain financial and delivery states, unfinished work, notification/acknowledgment, response/recovery times and the resulting useful output. The receiving engineer reopens the same history after restart, including observation gaps. The implementation follows Stellar's [threat-modeling guidance](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/security-docs/threat-modeling) and [builder monitoring template](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/security-docs/monitoring/monitoring-template-builders).

A completed purchase requires **one distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output**. Transactions are deduplicated per network; assets and fees remain separate. A prepaid pass counts once when its first agreed operation produces accepted output, with later calls retained as usage. Every agreed page/file or order action must be accepted before the customer task completes.

The original first attempt determines cohort membership. Settlement and accepted output must fall within the selected seven- or fourteen-day window; later observations keep their actual time. Attempted, complete, partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes remain visible. Two-facilitator comparisons hold service, schema, population and output constant.

Customer benefit compares the prior task, first installed execution and recurring use on equivalent source/output: active effort, corrections, elapsed time to accepted output and unresolved work. A stated-period labor calculation uses comparable hours saved and the customer's stated hourly value, less implementation and incremental provider, host, payment and support costs. Accepted milestones, actual collections and support effort remain alongside those inputs.

# Merchant financial reviewer walkthrough

Follow one merchant's useful service and original customer records from setup through payment, correction, account close and receiving. The finished handover explains what was sold, what the customer received, which money moved, what remains due and how the next operator continues the same work.

Use the actual selected merchant, customer, source files and account period throughout. The installed product keeps the original network transfers, commercial valuations, issued documents, bank observations and service activity available together. This guide follows the existing applications and their saved records.

## Choose the working edition and account

The public financial integration is [PR2583, merge 8aed042e](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/pull/2583). Its 139 changed paths join invoice collection, refunds, customer credit, bank receipts, payment plans, service agreements, customer closing and Xero with the original merchant accounting host. The same release exposes 46 receivables operations through the existing merchant MCP interface.

The maintained product also includes the complete [Bank statement reconciliation application](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/e57a359966f093f483a1aa5f4c2dac28566b6a5c/products/merchant-bank-statements/README.md), with original statement balances, fees, remittances and account-close editions. Select the complete maintained source that contains the applications needed for the chosen customer task. The package's manifest and saved Runtime review identify that source and its dependencies.

| Open in the installed product | Work performed | Original state to retain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Grant purchase reviewer | Open the existing paid example and read its complete saved result. | Purchase packet, quote identities, returned bytes and reviewer directory. |
| Merchant accounting | Review the merchant's original source, native transfer, delivery and reconciliation. | Accounting workspace, configured outbox, proofs, terms and saved report. |
| Merchant receivables | Issue the customer's invoice, receive or apply money, credit or refund, and continue collections. | Customer UUID, invoice and receipt records, dated allocations and original request IDs. |
| Customer payment plans and Xero customer handovers | Agree collection dates and receive the accountant's original document outcomes. | Same accounting workspace, schedule editions and Xero package family. |
| Bank statement reconciliation | Match actual bank movements, fees and existing customer money; retain a period close. | Original account and statement files, posting coverage and close editions. |
| Customer statements | Explain prepaid service activity and issue or resume the customer's closing cycle. | Original merchant connection, capture sources, saved cycle and complete customer packet. |

The accounting directory has one writer. Use the companion views of the running service together. To move that directory to another saved Application or a direct command, stop its current owner through the existing lifecycle and reopen the same directory. The customer-closing workbench uses the existing merchant MCP owner.

## Open the delivered customer billing case

The completed [portable customer handover](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/eaa169825c48c5ec3cef260672dc8fa52deb5e12/stellar/scf_2026/commercial_milestone_handover_20261012/PORTABLE.md) supplies a concrete starting account. Its version-1 archive retains the full 243-file application, the original native accounting workspace, both saved planning cases, customer working files and the portable opening/repacking commands. The original native and independent receiving operation completed on the desktop and 390-pixel customer billing views.

Use the delivered **SCF_Customer_Billing_Portable_Complete_20261012.zip** and its included openers. The complete archive is 11,158,060 bytes with SHA-256 **a1579acfd1a1ac9f6c3597fb7ed341d37257a9bcea8a5427a51875d59f6eb834**. On Linux with Python 3.11 or later and Node 22 or later:

~~~sh
python3 -B open-portable-commercial-handover.py inspect \
  /absolute/private/SCF_Customer_Billing_Portable_Complete_20261012.zip

python3 -B open-portable-commercial-handover.py open \
  /absolute/private/SCF_Customer_Billing_Portable_Complete_20261012.zip \
  --root /absolute/private/customer-billing \
  --sha256 a1579acfd1a1ac9f6c3597fb7ed341d37257a9bcea8a5427a51875d59f6eb834
~~~

The chosen root's parent must exist. Open the private access page printed by the launcher. Choose **Delivery operations → Customer billing**, the retained case and its **Freeform Solutions** schedule. Follow the original invoices, receipt and allocation:

| Original operated example | Retained outcome |
| --- | --- |
| First USD 4,400 milestone | Invoice Paid, original USD 4,400 receipt allocation, amount due 0. |
| Later USD 4,400 handover milestone | Invoice Open, amount due USD 4,400. |
| Planning and accounting receiving | Both original planning databases and the full account survived repack, independent cold receiving and reopening. |

Add **--case receiving** when opening to select the independently received planning case. Repeated opening continues the same private working root, including later edits. After closing its services, the original **repack** command produces the next complete edition from that current account and both planning databases. The linked portable guide includes the full receiving and later-move commands.

These saved values describe the completed customer operating example and its original account records. The application measures independent adoption and paid Stellar use through its existing customer and purchase registers.

## 1. Set up the merchant's installed workspace

Build the selected source through the existing distribution builder. This example selects the complete receivables, quotation, payment-plan and accountant workflow:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/merchant-checkout --ref FULL_COMMIT_SHA \
  --selection merchant-receivables-xero --out /private/finance-release
~~~

Retain the returned archive and SHA-256. Prepare and open it through the original runtime installer:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs prepare \
  --dir /private/finance-runtime \
  --archive /absolute/returned-package.tgz --sha256 RETURNED_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --native --feature schema --feature openapi --operator

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs install \
  --dir /private/finance-runtime

node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs inspect \
  --dir /private/finance-runtime --load --source
~~~

The installer selects the original declared package versions and retains their lock. Its `resume` operation continues an interrupted preparation. Use the [bank installation guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/e57a359966f093f483a1aa5f4c2dac28566b6a5c/products/merchant-bank-statements/INSTALLATION.md) when the chosen customer task includes that complete bank application.

The examples below use the installed `starforge` command. The installer runs the same command in its retained package layout:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs run \
  --dir /private/finance-runtime -- receivables help
~~~

For a new accounting workspace, select the merchant's actual source outbox, verification directory and accounting terms. Keep the state directory separate from those inputs:

~~~sh
starforge receivables serve \
  --directory /private/merchant/accounting \
  --outbox /private/merchant/source/outbox \
  --proof-dir /private/merchant/source/proofs \
  --terms /private/merchant/source/terms.json \
  --port 8448
~~~

For an existing account, retain its saved source configuration and open that same accounting directory. Open the URL printed at startup. In **Settings**, save the issuer's billing identity, document prefixes and payment instructions. In **Customers and statements**, select or create the actual customer, billing address and reference. Reuse that customer's UUID through the invoice, receipt and export.

To manage the installed application, use the original Runtime workspace:

~~~sh
starforge runtime-workspace init --workspace /private/finance-operator

starforge runtime-workspace attach \
  --workspace /private/finance-operator \
  --runtime /private/finance-runtime --label "Merchant finance"

starforge runtime-workspace serve \
  --workspace /private/finance-operator --port 8465
~~~

In **Applications**, review the installed runtime and original accounting directory, then **Save → Start → Open** the selected merchant application. **Xero customer handovers** serves its original invoice, payment-plan and customer-statement companion routes under that same accounting owner.

**Ready to continue:** the operator can identify the installed source, workspace UUID, actual input paths, issuer and selected customer in the application.

## 2. Start with the useful paid result

For the selected merchant's own demonstration, open the customer's recorded purchase in **Buyer results** and the matching original merchant accounting event. Review the exact source/query, agreed population or period, price, network, asset, result and fulfillment together.

The **grant-reviewer** selection supplies the already operated bundled reference for this opening step. Prepare that selected runtime through the same original builder and installer, with its own release and runtime directories, and attach it to the existing Runtime workspace. Its source command is:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/merchant-checkout --ref FULL_COMMIT_SHA \
  --selection grant-reviewer --out /private/grant-reviewer-release
~~~

Use the returned archive and source hash in the same prepare/install/inspect workflow above. In **Applications**, choose **Grant purchase reviewer** from that attached runtime, review its private workbench directory, then **Save → Connect → Start → Open**. The direct entry is:

~~~sh
starforge grant-demo workbench \
  --dir /private/merchant/grant-review --port 0
~~~

In **Packet intake**, choose **Review bundled purchase**. Open **Source and query**, then **Receive this packet → Open original Buyer → Buyer results**. Select each original quote and choose **Read complete saved result**.

The bundled successful HPD result contains 100 rows, 14 columns and 53,468 bytes; its retained truncation flag is true. The original 4,733-byte error result belongs to the earlier indeterminate quote and remains separately readable. A different completed Queens HPD acquisition received its full 144-row task in two paid pages. The [original reviewer guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/0c422d12288849eb38466b4e36e9288e4383d0e8/products/grant-reviewer/OPERATING.md) supplies the saved-packet and cold-receiving procedure.

In **Merchant accounting → Sources**, open the chosen merchant's actual outbox, verification files and accounting terms. **Reconcile current sources** retains a complete source snapshot. Open the resulting event, native transfer, full delivery record and customer/order binding.

Native asset units and merchant-supplied commercial valuation have their own fields. The original transaction fingerprint joins the transfer on its selected network. A saved output, another read of it and a later customer statement continue that same purchase.

**Ready to continue:** the useful output opens completely, and its recorded commercial and native identities are visible in the original purchase and accounting records.

## 3. Turn the accepted service into an issued invoice

An installation or service obligation begins with the customer's actual accepted scope. In **Merchant support**, open the original quotation and recorded response. Retain the complete quotation and its selected response files.

In **Invoices and payments**, import those originals, map the accounting customer and choose the intended charge. **IMPLEMENTATION** selects the one-time lines. **RECURRING** selects the original recurring lines with an explicit positive period count and period label. An accepted service-agreement calendar can prepare the original period's draft through the same invoice writer.

Review the quote edition, customer response, quantities, unit prices, discounts, taxes, commercial currency and decimal precision. The issue date, due date and service period answer different questions and stay explicit. The source review retains the original quote lines, calculations and rounding differences. A manual invoice uses the same complete review with the operator's actual supporting source.

If this merchant enabled **Customer credit**, inspect the saved policy and current assessment before release. The decision shows the selected draft alongside the customer's current and future obligations, overdue or disputed balances, and available receipts. Record the actual decision and reason. The invoice issue uses that reviewed account and policy basis.

**Save draft → Review → Issue** freezes the numbered invoice with the issuer, customer, dates, payment instructions and exact amounts. Download its original JSON, line CSV, printable HTML and manifest. Later account changes remain visible alongside that issued document.

**Ready to continue:** the invoice has its original number and files, retained source/acceptance, actual dates and a dated amount due.

## 4. Receive the payment against the original obligation

Choose the route the customer actually used. The receipt records received money; an allocation states how much of that receipt applies to an invoice and from which date. The unused portion remains in that customer's account.

### Stellar wallet collection

In the invoice's **Stellar payment requests**, select the part of the balance to collect. Review the merchant destination, network, asset and issuer, memo, expiry and payer constraint when selected.

`invoiceAmount` is the commercial value applied to the invoice. `stellarAmount` is the exact transferred asset amount, at up to seven decimal places. Preserve the agreed `valuationNote` whenever those units differ.

Issue the reviewed request and open its original **payment-request.html** and **payment-request.uri**. The customer reviews and signs those terms in their selected wallet. Record the returned transaction hash against that issued request, then choose **Receive**.

The original verifier checks the network, successful operation, destination, asset, received amount, memo and ledger time. Fee-bump outer and inner hashes remain aliases of the same transfer. Public-network receiving retains the original customer receipt and eligible allocation; the test-network path displays its original **TESTNET_VERIFIED** observation and proof.

If a payer or invoice reference was entered incorrectly before verification, use the original noted correction in that saved return and inspect the resulting history. The reported transaction stays in its original record. A verified or receipted transfer retains its established financial assignment.

### Bank payment or another recorded receipt

Open the original receipt or source payment first. Retain the actual received date, method, reference, currency and amount. Select the invoice and its allocation amount and effective date.

A bank observation that refers to an already recorded payment matches that receipt. A customer payment spanning several invoices uses explicit allocations; a bank credit spanning several customers uses the original reviewed split-posting flow in **Bank statements**.

When a completed native accounting event supplies the receipt, select that original report/event and retain its network, transaction, asset and atomic amount alongside the chosen commercial valuation.

**Ready to continue:** the receipt, original source, invoice allocation and remaining customer funds agree at the selected accounting date. The source and invoice remain downloadable.

## 5. Return customer funds or move paid credit

Open **Customer funds** for the same customer and currency. Select the original receipt, the actual reason and the intended refund or credit movement. The preview shows allocated, reserved, refunded and available amounts before and after the proposal.

A credit note changes the issued charge. Select the original invoice lines and explicit net/tax amounts, review and issue the credit. When an already paid invoice is credited, the original paid allocation may need a dated release before the receipt can fund the refund or another invoice. The desk reviews that release and any remaining replacement allocation as one conserved change.

For a completed refund, record its actual method, reference and payment date. For a **Stellar wallet** refund, review the merchant paying account, customer destination, network, asset and exact value before issuing the retained wallet request. Reserved customer funds and the later verified payment remain visible in the original request history. The original verified payout or refund-adjustment path can receive a payment that already has native proof.

**Move credit** applies the same retained customer receipt to selected outstanding invoices. Review the target amounts and dates. Any remainder stays available in the account.

A corrected recorded refund retains the original reversal and linked replacement. The actual payment date and effective accounting correction can differ; inspect both. Saved refund files contain the original receiving record, customer documents and native proof.

**Ready to continue:** the customer account explains the credit, released or replaced allocations, refund or transfer, remaining funds and every original source record.

## 6. Reconcile the bank period

Open the selected original bank account and actual statement period. The receivables **Bank statements** desk and the maintained **Bank statement reconciliation** application use the same payment/source relationships. The installed bank selection opens **/bank-statements/**; its companion invoice, customer and payment-plan views share that original accounting owner. Select **Remittance receiving** at **/receivables/remittances.html** for a customer's complete payment-and-invoice allocation CSV.

Receive the complete CSV, OFX/QFX or selected MT940 source through its original parser. Review the actual account section, currency, date convention, opening/closing information and parser report. CSV uses an explicit column mapping. MT940 retains its selected envelope, encoding, debit/reversal convention, year window and value-date basis.

Match each source movement to the existing receipt, refund or other cash record. For new customer money, review the complete split and original invoice allocations. A partial correction preserves the other source portions and the customer's remaining receipt.

The documented bank workflow can match a 97.00 bank credit to a 100.00 customer receipt plus a separate -3.00 fee in the same currency. The invoice keeps its 100.00 payment allocation. That gross/net relationship remains explicit in the bank posting instead of changing the original customer charge.

Use the retained account and inclusive period to review its close. Inspect opening balance plus selected posted movements against the actual closing balance, together with outstanding matching and source work. Retain the reviewed close with its transaction/posting CSVs, original statements, readable reconciliation, editable account data and customer exports.

A later correction reopens the affected close and creates a reviewed successor. Earlier close files remain available. The original bank operation reported a 150.00 close and its corrected 155.00 successor; the [worked account guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/e57a359966f093f483a1aa5f4c2dac28566b6a5c/products/merchant-bank-statements/EXAMPLE.md) identifies that same example and its original sources.

**Ready to continue:** the reviewer can trace a bank row through exact posting coverage to customer money and a retained account-close edition.

## 7. Schedule and follow up the remaining balance

In **Payment plans**, select the issued invoice and actual balance date. Enter the agreed dates and exact installment amounts, or use **Generate installments** and edit its proposed dates.

Save the draft, inspect the full account basis and activate the reviewed edition. Each edition retains **schedule.html**, **schedule.csv**, **schedule.json** and **manifest.json**. Earlier customer schedules stay readable after a replacement or dated cancellation.

The collection view separates overdue, due-today, upcoming, after-horizon, unscheduled and credit balances by currency and precision. Effective payments cover the earlier remaining installments; credits reduce later amounts; releases restore their original invoice amount. The schedule distributes the existing obligation across dates.

Use **Collections** for the invoice's actual owner, follow-up, customer contact, promise and dispute history. **Cash planning** combines the retained remaining invoices, effective schedules and original promises into a reviewed dated scenario. Inspect changed source bases, assumptions and available customer funds before saving it.

**Ready to continue:** the selected schedule and follow-up explain when the original remaining amount is expected, with the actual receipt and issued balance still available.

## 8. Close the customer's account and service period

### Dated invoice account

Choose the actual as-of date. Review issued invoices, credit notes, received funds, effective allocations/releases, refunds and available credit. Keep each currency and precision separate. A historical view uses its effective dates while later corrections remain in history.

Download the complete dated customer account, including original issued documents, receipt advice, correction relationships and allocation history. The recipient can trace the selected balance to those files.

### Prepaid service closing

In **Customer statements**, use the original running merchant MCP address, accounting alias, named operator and saved closing directory. The installed direct entry is:

~~~sh
starforge customer-closing \
  --directory /private/merchant/customer-closes \
  --url http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp \
  --workspace accounting --actor operator --port 4419
~~~

The actual merchant connection and access-token environment are retained by the configured application. Open **Customers and service** to inspect the customer's original order assignments and imported service captures.

In **Compose a cycle**, choose the customer, completed accounting run and original opening/closing captures for each pass. Inspect the capture times and period, review the native statement and prepare the saved cycle. Issue it through the original requests, or resume the saved cycle when an earlier reply was interrupted.

Open the issued statement's original files and current lifecycle. A correction keeps the selected statement, customer, source and period linked to its replacement. A withdrawal retains its reason and earlier files.

**Download customer delivery** gives the complete available customer packet. The whole-cycle download keeps the operator's full saved work for another receiving engineer. The packet's register shows completed statements and any remaining rows in that same cycle.

**Ready to continue:** the customer has the dated money account and the original service-period explanation, with separate financial and usage records joined by their real identities.

## 9. Receive the accountant's Xero outcome

In **Xero customer handovers**, use the receiving organisation's actual invoice/credit templates and saved contact, account, tax, currency and date-format mapping. Select the original issued documents and account date, then **Review selected documents → Prepare immutable package**.

Download the original import files and source package for the accountant's established receiving workflow. Retain document numbers, mapping edition and package identity.

Receive the complete original Xero **Invoices** or **CreditNotes** JSON response from that organisation. The desk retains its returned document UUIDs, exact numeric tokens, status, validation results and source pointers. A supplied summary CSV uses its explicitly selected mapping and number/sign conventions.

Open unresolved, rejected, mismatched or conflicting documents with their actual returned reason. Use an eligible linked correction and receive the resulting original outcome. Accepted external identities and all prior returns remain available in the package family.

The Xero status describes that document handover. The merchant's received and refunded money continues through its original receipts, allocations and native/bank sources.

## 1. Customer problem and commercial model

An API or data-service operator needs to expose a useful resource to agent applications while retaining access rules, source meaning and commercial control. A buyer needs the complete result it approved and a way to resolve an interrupted paid request. The difficult join spans four records: approved request, settled transfer, delivered output and accepted fulfillment or accounting.

Current x402 reports show the practical need for that join. One October 2 report described payment-bearing requests rejected because a merchant required POST while the reference client retried GET; health and catalogue checks had appeared normal. The author subsequently corrected the server. An October 3 report described settlement without a discovery listing; a separate operator later reported successful indexing of its own resources and explained the facilitator diagnostics in that thread. These were Base deployments. They show how a healthy catalogue or settled payment can leave the customer's task unfinished. Our Stellar implementation retains the exact request and each original outcome so the unfinished step can be recovered. [Method report](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/3657) · [Discovery report](https://github.com/x402-foundation/x402/issues/3677)

We serve recurring API/data-service operators, the developers using their results and agencies commissioned to integrate them. A fixed-fee implementation delivers one agreed operation and a handover the receiving engineer can maintain. Further care has its own scope. The commissioning payer, merchant controlling the resource and independent buyer may be different organizations. The workorder names each role, its source and host authority, payment responsibility and acceptance owner. The merchant retains its API or product receipts; TokenJunkieLabs invoices the implementation.

The selected customer task and the priced unit are recorded together. A complete report may require several paid pages. A handover may contain many files or transport chunks. The buyer retains per-request and aggregate spending controls while the operating record shows whether the whole task is complete. A later reporting period, changed source edition, fresh query or new order gives the same buyer a reason to use the service again.

## 2. Product architecture and control

Six connected components form the application: the merchant's private source/release workspace; its HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and configured facilitator; the buyer's private approval and spending state; complete result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Merchant and buyer services run on their operators' hosts. Approved operations are public; administration, provider credentials, signer references and operating state stay private.

| Stage | Implemented customer control |
| --- | --- |
| Review and publish | Review a source edition or named live query, its arguments and schema, public fields, output limits and complete payment alternatives. Save rights, route, network, asset, recipient, atomic amount and authorization lifetime. Changes or withdrawal become new reviewed states. |
| Connect the source | Preserve original types, missing/null values, pagination and snapshot/live meaning. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth aliases select access and the existing quota/cache state. Retain the edition behind each result. |
| Approve and purchase | Save the actual endpoint, method or tool, arguments, payment option and result scope. Match remote schema and challenge to that selection before signing. Keep the per-payment ceiling and the application's aggregate reservation/budget owner. |
| Settle and deliver | Use the configured native SDK/facilitator for verification and settlement. Save the server's response, full output, byte identity and durable merchant notification. Independently reconcile transaction network, asset, payer, payee and atomic amount. |
| Use and maintain | Receive every selected page or file into the customer's existing application, query, report or workbook. Preserve the parent acquisition and earlier source editions. Existing order and finance authorities control fulfillment, refunds and accounting. |
| Deploy and receive | Select the release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. Drain, restart, roll back and restore with the original configuration, history and complete customer files. |

The native x402 flow reuses the existing Exact Stellar scheme, token contracts and facilitator supported/verification/settlement interfaces. For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments remain distinct from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge; the full payment option must match the saved quote before the signed call is dispatched. The official MCP SDK transports the payment and settlement metadata.

Server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete useful output, receiver acknowledgment and order fulfillment remain separately visible. An uncertain signed reply retains its dispatch state for reconciliation. Reopening a consumed quote returns saved work. Recovery of a complete retained result uses that saved result. A new request or changed purchase gets its own review. Complete export and restore carry the configuration, history and referenced files; the receiving host supplies current authorized secret references.

Browser, CLI, MCP and installed Applications use these same saved workspaces. Native source registrations connect setup, operation and lifecycle while preserving each source adapter's data semantics. The existing request-collection, buyer-to-Operations and document-analysis extensions retain their own original recovery operations; their pending native receiving stages are reported separately from the completed examples below.

Stellar settles the approved operation. Buyer approval binds the complete request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. ## 7. Threat response and useful-outcome measurement

T2 includes the actual deployment's threat assessment, monitoring thresholds, notification destinations, accountable responders and material remediation.

| Failure to operate | Control and observation |
| --- | --- |
| Changed source, request or terms | Match exact source generation, request and approved payment alternative before dispatch. Retain rejection cause, quote age, source expiry and capacity refusal. |
| Uncertain payment or incomplete delivery | Reconcile the original intent and transfer, retain partial output/entitlement state and recover unfinished work. Measure outstanding age and time to useful output. |
| Unauthorized access or exposed private state | Validate issuer, audience, subject, scopes, expiry and current authority. Restrict administration and protect credentials, keys, claim tokens, private bodies and backups; retain access/rotation observations. |
| Observation or notification failure | Keep the last useful capture, incident and original notification attempts. Retry the same event; measure coverage, alert, acknowledgment and recovery time. |
| Restart or state loss | Restore the selected backup and reconcile later operations. Reopen the same support case and full output on the receiving host; measure time, retained history and active effort. |

## Customer value and delivery economics

Evaluate the complete task and its recurrence. Let F be the one-time implementation fee, V the customer’s stated value of an hour, H the measured active hours saved per equivalent completed task, N the number of useful repeat tasks, and C the period’s incremental provider, hosting, payment and support cost. The direct labor-value comparison is `N × H × V − F − C`; the effort reduction per task needed to recover the fee is `(F + C) / (N × V)`.

The following planning example assumes twelve monthly tasks and zero entered incremental costs. The two hourly values are explicit scenarios for the customer to replace with its own value; the prior and installed tasks must retain comparable source scope and usable output.

|$4,800|$125|38.40|3.20|
|$7,200|$75|96.00|8.00|
|$7,200|$125|57.60|4.80|

### The operator and buyer journey

An operator connects to the merchant's invoice desk with the private operator token, enters a business reference and description, and selects exact prices on the configured payment rails. **Create payment request** retains the original charge and produces a downloadable wallet request containing the unchanged payment requirement and protected request. The buyer's compatible wallet integration returns the complete authorization. The operator can receive that authorization, or the buyer can submit the original protected request directly. The server retains the authorization before making its first empty upstream payment POST. Payment refresh and recovery continue that invoice and its original request.

The service receives the configured ownership challenge and authenticates webhook bytes before interpreting their payload. It verifies a finalized receipt using separately configured signing-key fingerprints and the invoice's original payment, order, resource and selected price bindings. The browser does not hold the tenant credential or webhook secrets. The operator token remains in browser memory and is cleared on disconnect; server credentials continue to use the deployment's existing environment references.

Once the selected payment is verified, the configured fulfillment adapter supplies the useful result. The original file adapter returns the exact content-bound file edition; it retains earlier editions for earlier invoices. A customer-specific handler receives the original payment ID as its idempotency key and supplies its own authoritative reconciliation for external work. The application retains returned result bytes before publishing the complete file through the original SF31 writer. Every download uses the original SF88 verified-file reader to check the retained size and SHA-256.

The invoice desk exposes the saved request, payment and delivery progress, activity history, wallet request and completed download. The HTTP interface serves the same records used by the browser. Reopening an existing project keeps its completed invoices, authorizations, authenticated events, fulfillment records and original result files.

## Complete delivered-edition review and independent customer receiving

### Customer operation

The operator opens the delivered files in **Edition review**, selects before and after resources and chooses their interpretation. A comparison reads both complete verified files. JSON retains exact number literals, type changes and null-versus-missing distinctions. CSV uses explicit identity columns when supplied, preserving quoted cells and detecting duplicate identities. Text retains line endings; binary review identifies changed byte ranges. Searchable text prefixes are for discovery; the comparison and exact download use complete source files.

A saved comparison retains its source identities, direction, settings, complete change rows and every decision revision. |  ---  |  ---  |
|Receive an incoming handover into a comparison already under review.|The incoming source is retained. Compatible newer decisions append; older input preserves newer local work. |Receive a complete journal with earlier sources, staged returns and reconciliation receipts.|The operator stages it against the current local journal, inspects the histories and explicitly keeps local work, takes the returned decision or authors a new resolution. |Continue in a separate customer workspace.|The recipient imports the full comparison and journal, reviews earlier resolutions, saves a new decision and exports its next complete edition. Reopening selects the same saved comparison and history.|


Both receiving paths use the original decision writer. An intervening decision makes an older resolution plan stale so the operator reviews the current state before applying it. Applying a reviewed return is one transaction. Replaying an interrupted request uses its saved operation identity and returns the original outcome.       "markdown": "# Reviewer application\n\n**Stellar Discovery Trust Layer — TokenJunkieLabs — SCF #46 Build / Open Track**\n\n## Project and requested outcome\n\nTokenJunkieLabs builds open-source, self-hostable software that carries a paid API, dataset or agent operation through to completed customer work. A merchant publishes an authorized resource; a buyer approves the exact request and total spending, pays through Stellar, and receives the complete result in its application. The merchant retains the offer, fulfillment and accounting. Another engineer can restore the installation and continue its original work.\n\nWe request **$38,000 for 400 prospective development and technical integration hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance**. The funded outcome is **two independently operated merchant services used by two independent buyer operators**:\n\n* **Day 30:** both services installed with their authorized sources, receiving applications and accountable operators.\n* **Day 90:** at least ten useful testnet purchases during seven consecutive days, with both merchants represented; the same useful service operates through two independent facilitators.\n* **Day 150:** both merchants live on mainnet, with at least thirty useful purchases during fourteen consecutive days, both buyers returning on another UTC day, and completed recovery and independent maintainer handover.\n\nThe working product supplies the architecture, payments and source-to-customer foundation. The six packages below fund the selected installations' remaining source adapters, receiving integration, deployment, monitoring and recovery. Reusable improvements return to the public product; completed pre-award work remains the starting point.\n\n## Customer problem, need and adoption\n\nOur initial users are recurring API/data-service operators and the agencies integrating their services into customer applications. The commissioning payer buys implementation and handover; the merchant earns resource receipts; the independent buyer purchases useful output. These roles may belong to different organizations.\n\nA paid response must become a usable customer result: every required page or file, the correct population and period, original units and types, and an output that opens in the receiving application. An interrupted request also needs a clear financial and delivery outcome. These requirements are especially important when an agent makes several paid requests to complete one task.\n\nWe support two recurring installation patterns:\n\n|Customer task|Accepted output|\n|  ---  |  ---  |\n|Receive a new economic or operational reporting period, then compare it with the previous edition.|Complete report and underlying selection, retaining units, periods, source editions and review decisions.|\n|Run an approved typed query or acquire a refreshed dataset.|Every agreed page/file, with the exact request, source selection, aggregate cost and merchant record.|\n\n\n**The two funded installations and customer agreements are still being selected.** Current human conversations give concrete commissioning conditions: Veridex invited the buyer CLI into its testnet cohort and reported no third-party testing budget; CoCart's founder asked who introduces, pays and contracts for customer work; Blockscout expressed interest without an integration budget; Nansen declined. These are relationship outcomes, separate from paid customer adoption.\n\nEach selected workorder will name the payer, source owner, merchant, independent buyer, integration and receiving engineers, host and acceptance owner. It will specify the authorized population/period/query, useful output, advertised paid unit, aggregate spending limit and responsibility for hosting and purchases. An installed baseline and a later genuinely needed period, edition or query establish recurring demand. Source permission, operator availability and the complete customer task are settled before its deployed work begins.\n\nThe delivered economic, Timescale, aid-data and scientific-array applications provide concrete candidates for these two patterns. Existing proposed workshares retain their original source, effort, fees and customer conditions in the detailed application. For example, the GeoRobotix observation-source proposal is **$9,600 / 72 engineering hours / twelve active business days**, with two $4,800 milestones. Its first offer was sent on October 13 at 00:05:31 UTC; delivery starts after source selection, access and the receiving environment are ready. Its reusable illustrative-source workflow has completed review, query/export, separate receiving and cold reopen. The commercial case has separately completed scope planning, independent receiving and the maintained Installation intake; its eight engineering workorders remain planned. Customer installation, live collection and the paid Stellar service remain prospective.\n\nThe purchase target follows actual work. Two buyers making one purchase per weekday would produce only twenty purchases in fourteen days. The chosen T3 work must therefore require at least thirty distinct useful paid requests across both buyers and merchants. Advertised pages can be separate purchases within one complete task; replay, reopening and cached use retain the original purchase. The existing Customer-use Calendar links the saved Installation, buyers, complete tasks and funding groups to the original purchase observations.\n\nTokenJunkieLabs earns separately agreed implementation and care fees. Merchants retain resource revenue and implementation partners retain customer relationships. Each adaptation, delivery hour and support obligation is allocated once between the grant and commissioned work.\n\n## Why Stellar and what we contribute\n\nStellar supplies authorization and settlement for the selected purchase. In the existing x402 Exact flow, the buyer signs token-transfer authorization binding payer, recipient, atomic amount and expiration. A facilitator submits it on the selected network; fee sponsorship can cover the transaction fee. We use existing Stellar SDKs and token contracts.\n\nOur application binds that transfer to the exact HTTP request or MCP tool/arguments, selected source, payment option, complete customer output and fulfillment history. The buyer controls wallet authority and total spend; the merchant controls source access, pricing and fulfillment.\n\nThe ecosystem already supplies substantial infrastructure. Stellar's x402 client libraries handle payment challenges, Soroban authorization and signed retries; the Stellar CLI supplies the signing identity. Facilitators verify and settle, and Bazaar describes discoverable resources. ApiCharge's published proxy/access-grant approach provides typed paid access and retained purchased service levels. MPP Router provides paid proxy access, request-ID response caching and signed job polling. Our Open Track contribution is the complete recurring customer operation built on those foundations: reviewed source and query, aggregate approval, every agreed page/file, editable output, interrupted-delivery recovery, accounting and independent maintenance.\n\nThe programme makes that contribution measurable. It installs two independent services and buyers, operates the same useful service through two testnet facilitators, and carries both merchants into recurring mainnet use. The two-provider comparison holds the service, schema, source population and useful output constant. Existing catalogs do not by themselves establish this compatibility: the retained Vellar/Periplo comparison found no shared seller/route identity, so explicit registration and integration of the same service is part of the funded work.\n\n[Stellar x402](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/build/agentic-payments/x402/built-on-stellar) · [Stellar agent payment guide](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/guides/pay-for-apis-x402) · [ApiCharge protocol](https://apicharge.com/Documentation/core-concepts.html) · [MPP Router](https://www.mpprouter.dev/llms.txt). The detailed application retains the full business and technical comparison.\n\n## Defined architecture and operating behavior\n\nThe architecture is defined and implemented across six components:\n\n|Component|Responsibility|\n|  ---  |  ---  |\n|**Merchant workspace**|Select authorized source/query, schema, output, price and limits. Retain separately reviewed source and terms changes or withdrawal.|\n|**HTTP or MCP resource**|Preserve types, nulls, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live semantics. Use customer-controlled source credential references.|\n|**Buyer approval and budget**|Approve exact method/tool, arguments, scope and payment option; match the challenge and schema before signing. Reserve aggregate task spending alongside per-payment limits.|\n|**Stellar settlement**|Use the reviewed network, asset, recipient, amount, expiry and fee policy. Independent customer deployments and mainnet use are the funded next stage.\n\n**Complete recurring dataset receiving.** All **830 original OData Orders** passed through typed collection, saved SQL, a report, a two-sheet workbook and independent analytical receiving. The same source definition produced zero row changes, retained as the actual result. The separate managed selection built and loaded all twelve entry points; managed preparation/adoption and Review → Start → receive → Stop → reopen remain to be operated on that completed customer edition.\n\n**A real Stellar purchase with a useful output.** Two 10,000-stroop purchases completed one **144-row Queens HPD customer task**, received as pages of 100 and 44 rows and reopened as CSV/JSONL with original source and accounting. A separate 50,000-stroop purchase returned 100 rows and fourteen columns, retained its original truncation flag, and reopened with signing disconnected and in another directory. Reviewers can inspect the [original acquisition record](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/687ea12ac97f06b7f1336676249c349ade7a7692/products/merchant-workspace/DEVELOPMENT.md#5-existing-delivery-foundation-and-receiving-examples), [reviewer operating guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/03a93f7c59a703ebc63416ae0e914f07099fef37/products/grant-reviewer/OPERATING.md) and [3:32 product/team film](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/public-commons-sprint-2026/releases/download/scf-presentation-20261011/stellar-forge-scf46-presentation.mp4).\n\n**Independent restoration and handover.** The OData receiver restored and continued the original subscription. [Saved prepaid passes](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/24506172ed7c4288d158ab7f6c1735c645dc6ab9/operations/api-pass-portfolio-agent-921ba0-20261012/NATIVE_RESULT.json) preserved each call’s selected pass and consumed allowance through replay and cold receiving. The [OpenLineage customer operation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/blob/1b1f756587619d21cab44f627f5d4e9b4fa6ad72/products/openlineage/OPERATING.md) let another engineer reopen accepted measurements, reports and history. Installation, recurring requests, bank statements and customer service closing retain their original operating and financial records. The complete Resource Review operation also received a conflicting reviewer return, applied the reviewed resolution, exported its full journal and continued editing after independent receiving without the original source files. Twelve desktop and phone views completed with no recorded page or console errors. Its [merged customer continuation](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/835) connects the Python entry, exact comparison and originating return to that full review.\n\nDiscovery also has a measured baseline against the actual 27-resource Vellar testnet catalog: schema-aware ranking retrieved all 31 declared query-resource relationships versus 22 previously, with matching direct/indexed results across 33 queries. The [detailed product companion](./product-and-finance.md) preserves the full product inventory, source populations, operating outcomes and remaining deployment steps. Selected customer source/roles, deployed purchasing/recovery and production handover remain within the existing T1, T2 and T3 packages.\n\nThe Human Services Directory has also completed its original native source-to-referral and independent receiving operation: twenty mapped fields, three resulting FHIR resources, retained warnings and service-selection classification, an explicit referral join and the full editable customer workspace. Its merged Operating Plans and declared-relationship operator extend the same source and customer workflow. The Directory chapter connects that delivered foundation to the existing source-specific T1 installation, T2 paid operation and T3 recurring-use/handover packages.\n\nThe Installation receiver-to-owner workflow also completed its full team-operated receiving: a receiver’s named observations return to the owner for explicit KEEP/APPLY decisions, changed criteria require a fresh review, and the next Installation edition remains editable. This demonstrates the handover and correction mechanism that T1 authority/handover and T3 recovery will configure for the two future customer installations.\n\n**Named-staff operating result.** The completed staff workflow operated six profiles, three work records and two example invoices through contribution, review, payment and correction. Fifteen desktop/mobile browser views completed without errors. The independently restored installation retained and verified all 421 source files, and reopened the original business history after a cold restart.\n\n## Three funded tranches and six priced deliverables\n**Day zero is actual award acceptance; the planning rate is $95/hour.** The same selected sources, useful tasks and independent operators continue through installation, testnet and mainnet.\n\n|Deadline and package|Remaining funded implementation|Hours / amount|Completion outcome|\n|  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |  ---  |\n|**T1, day 30 — Merchant-resource integration**|Customer source/runtime adapters, native resource routes, terms and typed receiving integration for both services.|**80 / $7,600**|Both independent merchants operate on their hosts; each buyer receives the complete agreed output with original source meaning and payment selection. Package completion includes the corresponding documentation and receiving changes so the next operator can use the delivered capability.\n\n## Threat response and outcome measurement\nT2 delivers a threat model, corresponding installed monitoring plan and material corrections.
